A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same prompt-space and answer-space analysis and experiments despite the changed title. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM prompting experiments, including structured reasoning results, CoT/ToT/GoT comparisons, tokenization experiments, and case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Tables 1–4 and the appendix case studies. Moving the large-scale results into the appendix does not change their status.

M1.justification: The prompting procedures remain unchanged: v1 Figures 6–14 match v2 Figures 9–17. The new prompt-selection discussion explains the existing approach without introducing an algorithm, model component, or changed inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same structured reasoning tasks, nine-task API suite, tokenization conditions, and Even Pairs and Reverse List examples. No dataset, task, or tested input environment is added or removed.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the same no-CoT, unsupervised CoT, supervised and suboptimal prompting conditions, ToT, and GoT. The RNN, Tape-RNN, and Transformer reference results are also retained.

E3.justification: The models, input lengths, four prompt conditions, 50-instance web evaluations, and 1,000-instance API table cells remain unchanged. The revised total of 144,000 rather than 36,000 API calls accounts for the four prompt conditions already displayed in v1; it does not establish an expanded evaluation.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same optimal-versus-suboptimal prompting comparisons, input-length evaluations, tokenization analysis, and six case-study responses. The added conceptual diagrams and computational-depth discussion introduce no new empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Both report average single-trial performance across instances; that explanation moves from Section 4.1 to Appendix B. Neither version reports seed variation, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical result tables and case-study outputs match after accounting for the exchanged Table 2 and Table 3 numbering. However, v1 Appendix A.5 describes reversing sequences up to 40 tokens as relatively successful, while v2 Appendix A.4 instead identifies duplication as successful on longer inputs. This revises a qualitative finding while retaining the underlying results.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 changes the assumed dependence of stored information from hidden-state dimension alone to dimension and task. Appendix E adds an explicit computational-depth definition and architectural characterizations, largely elaborating the existing depth argument. The binomial prompt-space count and answer-space ratio remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: v2 emphasizes a theoretical foundation for explaining and choosing prompt designs, whereas v1 foregrounds the necessity of human supervision. Its abstract also adds an explicit claim of over 50% improvement. The central claim that prompt selection governs answer-space reasoning remains intact.

C2.justification: Appendix E makes the depth argument more explicitly about per-token computation and short answer-only outputs. Section 2.3 also drops v1's assertion that Turing completeness permits solving any problem. The empirical generalization limitations and warnings about harmful supervision remain.

D1.justification: The embedded artifact link changes from an anonymous repository to a named GitHub repository. Appendix B also corrects total API-call accounting to 144,000 and explicitly enumerates the four prompt conditions. The detailed prompts and per-cell sample counts were already supplied in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds background citations, including Kahatapitiya et al. (2023), Wei et al. (2025), and several You et al. papers, and removes Boolos et al. (2002) and Jin et al. (2024). It emphasizes prompt-engineering foundations while retaining the existing positioning relative to CoT, ToT, GoT, and prompt-search research.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, substantial introduction passages, and conclusion are rewritten around two explicit research questions. v2 expands answer-token/helper-token explanations, adds Section 5 and Appendix E, consolidates Appendix A's length discussion, and moves experimental exposition into Appendix B.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands Figure 3, adds three explanatory diagrams as Figures 4–6, and revises labels and annotations in other conceptual figures. The large-scale results table moves into the appendix, changing the main-text presentation substantially while preserving its numerical contents.

improvement.justification: v2 improves explanatory clarity through expanded information-flow diagrams and a more explicitly scoped computational-depth discussion. It also resolves the API-call accounting inconsistency and supplies a named artifact address. These are useful presentation and documentation gains, while the experimental evidence and generalization limitations remain essentially unchanged.
